heroDescription: 89,853 g/t silver over 0.3m ranks among the richest silver intercepts ever drilled. Initial resource of 7.56 million ounces at 8,582 g/t established from two vein sections. December 2025 independent NI 43-101 technical report by Ronacher McKenzie Geoscience consolidates the 2011–2023 drill campaign and recommends further work to expand the mineralized footprint.
reportTitle: Castle Silver Property — Ronacher McKenzie Geoscience
milestoneItem1Description: 43,000m completed. Multiple new vein structures identified.
milestoneItem2Description: 89,853 g/t, 70,380 g/t, 50,583 g/t silver. 2.24% cobalt intercepts.
milestoneItem3Description: Multi-year data collection complete for permitting.
milestoneItem4Description: Design to 400m level complete. Awaiting updated resource.
milestoneItem5Description: 3D vein model with EarthLabs AI targeting.
milestoneItem6Description: Gravity recovery validated at TTL. Advanced hydrometallurgical testing underway.
rampDescription: Planned ramp provides platform for resource expansion drilling and bulk sampling. Engineering complete. Environmental studies submitted. Construction pending resource update and project financing.
historyTitle: First major discovery in camp since 1970s
historyDescription: Located 2km east of Castle Mine in unexplored gap. Historic producers Castle, Capitol, O'Brien combined for 80 million ounces from this structural trend.
geologyDescription: Mineralization occurs mid-level in the Nipissing diabase along its contact with overlying Huronian metasediments and underlying Archean volcanics, dipping east from the historic mines. A shallow intercept of 4,000+ g/t at 50m points to multiple mineralized horizons. The December 2025 NI 43-101 technical report integrates magnetic, DCIP and magnetotelluric surveys with 3D modelling to refine vein orientations, lithological domains and structural controls across the property.
figuresDescription: Reproduced from the December 2025 independent NI 43-101 technical report by Ronacher McKenzie Geoscience, these figures place the Robinson Zone discovery and adjacent target areas within the Castle East property's historic workings and Nipissing diabase host stratigraphy.
figure1Caption: Figure 1 — Plan view of modelling areas and historical workings (Castle–Trethewey, Capitol, Bonsall, and Millerette – Miller Lake – O'Brien). Scale 1:15,000, UTM NAD83 Zone 17.
figure2Caption: Figure 2 — Schematic section view (vertical exaggeration) showing the Robinson Zone, the historically mined favourable contact zone, and the BMR Gowganda East target zone within Huronian sediments, Archean volcanics, and the Nipissing diabase.
figuresFootnote: Figures prepared by G. Vernoux, P.Geo., supervised by M. Bouchard, P.Geo. (May 2026).
quote: The vein structures at Castle East show remarkable continuity. We're seeing the same high grades over significant distances, which is unusual for the camp and suggests a major mineralizing event.
silverDescription: Current resource from only two vein sections (1A and 1B) of Robinson Zone. Eight total structures identified. 2km strike length between Castle East and Castle Mine remains largely untested.
goldDescription: Gold values up to 22 g/t intersected in both diabase and overlying Archean rocks. Cobalt grades to 2.24%. Nickel and copper provide additional credits.
estimateNote2: Mineral resources are not mineral reserves. Economic viability not demonstrated.
estimateNote3: Resource basis: Rachidi, M. 2020, NI 43-101 Technical Report, effective May 28, 2020. Most recent independent disclosure: Enright & Ronacher, Ronacher McKenzie Geoscience Inc., effective December 3, 2025.
info1Description: Initial discovery at 427m vertical depth: 50,583 g/t Ag over 0.6m. Follow-up wedge holes confirmed continuity with 70,380 g/t and record 89,853 g/t intercepts.
info2Description: Systematic 25-50m spacing established 7.56M oz in 27,400 tonnes. Average grade of 8,582 g/t (250 oz/ton) ranks among world's highest silver resources.
